Research

Three questions connect my work.

01

How do economic forces shape identity and conflict?

02

How does economic connectivity create harmful spillovers?

03

How do governments and policies interact across firms and borders?

Ongoing work

Selected current projects.

Identity · Religious Diffusion

Religious Competition and the Limits of Islamic Diffusion in South Asia

with Jared Rubin and Avner Seror

A structural model of religious adoption in which co-religionist networks, inter-faith commerce, and political alignment shape religious diffusion across South Asia.

Identity · Conflict

How We Fight: Mineral Rents and the Composition of Conflict in India

with Raghul S. Venkatesh

We study whether mineral booms change not only the intensity of violence, but which forms of conflict become more salient.

Connectivity · Spillovers

Infectious Diseases, Livestock Losses, and Conflict

with Lore Vandewalle

We study whether infectious-disease shocks and associated livestock losses spill over into civil conflict, and how those effects propagate across space.

Government · Policy spillovers

Trade Exposure and Patterns of Industrial Policy Adoption

with Bernard Hoekman and Cosimo Beverelli

We examine how industrial-policy choices in one country relate to those adopted by its trading partners.

About

About me.

I am an Assistant Professor at the Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies at the European University Institute. I hold a PhD from the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies, where my dissertation received the Alumni Association Prize for the best thesis in Development Economics awarded during 2017–2023. I currently serve as an Associate Editor of the Journal of Economics, Management and Religion.
